labels.label: (prose, no label) colI_v1.tex l.742-744: elliptic, the angle
labels.notes: Uses the strict notions GX.PSL2.IsElliptic (trSq < 4, GX/BBS/RP1Circles.lean:979), GX.GTilde.IsElliptic and GX.GTilde.angle (2 pi times the translation number, RP1Circles.lean:1099). SL: GX.sl_exists_conj_slRot (A ~ rot(alpha), 0 < |alpha| < pi, conjugator in SL(2,R)). PSL: GX.PSL2.IsElliptic.exists_conj_slRot (0 < alpha < pi), and GX.PSL2.slRot_conj_iff makes alpha in (0, pi) a complete invariant. G~: GX.GTilde.isRotLift_angle (f = h R~(angle f) h^-1), GX.GTilde.exists_conj_of_angle_eq (same real angle => conjugate in G~) and the converse GX.GTilde.isConj_iff_angle_eq. Hypothesis is 'IsElliptic f or toPSL f = 1', exactly HSSingularities' form (central included, OQ-113 (d)); including central elements widens the statement, so Lean >= paper. No mark (no ledger label), correctly.

labels.label: (prose, no label) colI_v1.tex l.747-748: hyperbolic classes parametrised by |tr|
labels.notes: Uses GX.PSL2.IsHyperbolic (4 < trSq) and GX.PSL2.trSq. SL: GX.sl_exists_conj_slDiag (A = P diag(l, l^-1) P^-1, |l| > 1, l + l^-1 = tr A, P in SL(2,R)). PSL: GX.PSL2.IsHyperbolic.exists_conj_slDiag (l > 1). Injectivity: GX.PSL2.IsHyperbolic.exists_conj_of_trSq_eq; well-definedness and the iff: GX.PSL2.IsHyperbolic.isConj_iff_trSq_eq; l > 1 a complete invariant: GX.PSL2.slDiag_conj_iff. Surjectivity onto (2, oo) is not one declaration: GX.PSL2.isHyperbolic_slDiag only says diag(l, l^-1) is hyperbolic. The auditor checked that 'for every t > 2 there is a hyperbolic g with trSq g = t^2' follows in four lines from GX.exists_abs_gt_one_add_inv_eq, GX.PSL2.isHyperbolic_slDiag and GX.PSL2.trSq_pslMk_slDiag (scratch file, deleted), so the REPORT's 'every |tr| > 2 occurs' holds.

labels.label: (prose, no label) colI_v1.tex l.748-750: exactly two parabolic classes, positive and negative
labels.notes: Uses GX.PSL2.IsParabolic (trSq = 4, g != 1). SL: GX.sl_exists_conj_slUpper (tr^2 = 4, A not central => A ~ +-[[1, sigma], [0, 1]], sigma = +-1). PSL: GX.PSL2.IsParabolic.exists_conj_slUpper gives at most two classes. Both are parabolic (GX.PSL2.isParabolic_slUpper) and distinct (GX.PSL2.not_exists_conj_slUpper_one_neg_one), so there are exactly two. GX.PSL2.IsParabolic.isConj_iff_forall_le (parabolic g, g' are conjugate iff their lifts with a fixed point are both positive or both not) has the signature of HSSingularities' GX.PSL2.IsParabolic.isConj_iff. GX.GTilde.forall_le_iff_of_toPSL_conj_slUpper gives the sign: positive iff s < 0. The auditor confirmed the sign by hand: [[1, s], [0, 1]] sends [cos pi t : sin pi t] to cot(new angle) = cot(pi t) + s, so the fixed-point lift moves points up iff s < 0. Together with HSSingularities' GX.GTilde.IsParabolic.le_or_ge (positive or negative, not both), this is the paper's sentence. The reading of 'g x' for g in G as the lift with a fixed point is disclosed in SCOPE, the checklist and the REPORT's question. See minor finding 1 about the row's status.

question_check: The reading in the REPORT's question is sound. l.739 fixes g as the factor of rho(gamma_0) = delta^k g that has a fixed point in RP~1, while l.747 takes classes in G. The lift with a fixed point is unique (GX.GTilde.delta_zpow_mul_unique) and exists for a non-elliptic element (GX.GTilde.exists_delta_zpow_mul_of_not_isElliptic). Any other lift is delta^k f0 with k != 0. For k >= 1, f0 x + k > x - 1 + k >= x (FunnelGTilde's sub_one_lt_apply_of_fixed), so 'g x >= x' holds, strictly, for every parabolic element. For k <= -1, f0 x + k < x + 1 + k <= x (apply_lt_delta_of_fixed), so it fails at every point for every parabolic element. No reading through another lift gives two classes. The question is correctly a question, not a finding.
